title: Spin models with critical ground space degeneracy from Lie algebra relations
authors: Andras Molnar, Efekan Kökcü, Norbert Schuch, Bojko N. Bakalov
abstract: We introduce an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-symmetric spin model derived from the algebraic structure of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$: It is obtained as the nearest-neighbor parent Hamiltonian of a Matrix Product State (MPS) built from the generators of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and the identity matrix, and therefore encodes the quadratic relations of the Lie algebra. We characterize the ground space structure of the resulting model and show that for open boundary conditions (OBC), it exhibits a quadratic ground space degeneracy, given by one irreducible representation (irrep) of each odd dimension (integer spin). For periodic boundary conditions (PBC), it has a linear ground space degeneracy, consisting of a singlet --- namely, the MPS underlying the model --- and a ferromagnet (the irrep with maximal spin), and thus exhibits gapless excitations. We also generalize the construction and the analysis of the OBC ground space to $\mathrm{SO}(d)$ and other compact simple Lie groups.   The MPS on which the model is based is an injective MPS, and therefore, its 3-site parent Hamiltonian has a unique ground space and is gapped. The observed critical behavior thus has its origin in the small parent Hamiltonian considered. The model's algebraic ground space scaling thus provides an example distinct from that reported in (Schuch et al., 2025, arXiv:2503.10767), where it was shown that small parent Hamiltonians of injective MPS generically have unique ground states, and examples with an exponential ground space degeneracy were given.
summary: This work develops a method to study the ground state degeneracy of spin models by constructing them from the algebraic relations of Lie algebras, using Matrix Product States. For the $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ model, the authors find distinct ground state degeneracies depending on boundary conditions. This provides a novel, algebraically grounded understanding of critical quantum phases.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the ground space degeneracy of spin models derived from the algebraic structure of Lie algebras, specifically $\mathfrak{so}(3)$.
main_result: The model exhibits a quadratic ground space degeneracy for open boundary conditions (OBC) and a linear degeneracy for periodic boundary conditions (PBC).
method: The analysis uses the parent Hamiltonian derived from a Matrix Product State (MPS) built from the Lie algebra generators to determine the zero-energy eigenspace structure.
model_or_system: The system is an SO(3)-symmetric spin model whose Hamiltonian is constructed to encode the quadratic relations of the $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ Lie algebra. The analysis is generalized to other compact simple Lie groups.
key_observables: Ground space degeneracy (quadratic for OBC, linear for PBC), and the presence of gapless excitations in the PBC case.
important_parameters: The boundary conditions (OBC vs. PBC) and the specific Lie algebra ($\mathfrak{so}(3)$).
main_assumptions: The critical behavior is attributed to the parent Hamiltonian being a 'small' parent Hamiltonian, contrasting with generic injective MPS which usually yield unique ground states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the general framework of using MPS parent Hamiltonians to analyze ground space degeneracy, details the specific $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ case, and concludes with generalizations to $	ext{SO}(d)$ and other Lie groups.
why_interesting: The connection between algebraic structures (Lie algebras) and the ground state degeneracy of quantum spin models provides a powerful, symmetry-based tool for understanding critical behavior in strongly correlated systems.
